desc: Implement the complete `maximumWeight` solution: sort by `(r, l, idx)` carrying original indices; `prev[i]` via `bisect_left(rights, l_i)`; `better()` comparison (weight desc, then lex-smaller sorted tuple); 1-based DP over counts `0..4` with take/skip and sorted insertion of the original index; answer = best of `dp[n][0..4]`.

Test with both provided examples plus edge cases: single interval, all overlapping, boundary-touching intervals (must be rejected as overlapping), unsorted original indices vs right endpoints, equal weights requiring lexicographic tie-break, equal right endpoints, and fewer than 4 selectable intervals.

Write a brute-force verifier (exhaustive subsets up to size 4) and compare against the DP on random tiny inputs to confirm the per-state tie-break is globally correct — DP matched brute force on all fixed edge cases and 4000 randomized stress trials with heavy ties/touches.

Review complexity (`O(n log n)` time from sorting/binary searches, `O(5n)` DP transitions with constant-size tuples, `O(n)` memory) and finalize the method within the starter code — the `Solution.maximumWeight` implementation is complete, correct, and meets constraints for `n ≤ 5·10^4`.
